resharper_csharp_allow_alias #

Reference qualification and 'using' directives — Use using alias directive to resolve conflicts ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against jb cleanupcode 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified wrong subsystem — the arranger's. ⚠ Measured rather than filed by family resemblance, which is what the previous pass recorded it as. Flat at both values under the cleanup profile on a fixture where CSOptimizeUsings demonstrably removes three unused usings and shortens every reference to the SB alias. It governs whether a quick-fix may introduce an alias to resolve a conflict, which is an IDE action inside the arranger's half of the tool.

resharper_csharp_prefer_qualified_reference #

Reference qualification and 'using' directives — Prefer fully qualified references. ⚠ Not inert and not implemented. At true the oracle rewrites every simple name to its fully qualified form and drops the usings that become redundant; at the export's false it shortens an already-qualified reference — System.Text.StringBuilder becomes StringBuilder — which Skala does not do either. Skala has no reference-shortening rule, so the key is unreachable rather than unread. See SK-DIV-0073. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against jb cleanupcode 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified wrong subsystem — the arranger's. Confirmed: flat under CSReformatCode, two distinct outputs under the cleanup profile, where CSArrangeQualifiers performs it. SK-DIV-0073 stands.
